claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The baseline coating has a nominally homogeneous composition and microstructure.
A tailored annealing treatment or minor dopant addition can increase the coating's grain-boundary volume fraction.
Oxidation and thermally activated processes are significant during sliding at approximately 600–700°C.
Increasing grain-boundary volume fraction produces an enhanced grain-boundary network.
The enhanced grain-boundary network promotes preferential formation of a stable, continuous oxide layer along grain boundaries.
Greater grain-boundary volume facilitates localized oxidation during elevated-temperature sliding.
The resulting oxide films form protective barriers that reduce direct sliding contact.
Protective oxide films hinder grain-boundary sliding.
The modified coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited baseline.
The modified coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation, including reduced plastic flow and less evidence of grain-boundary sliding.
The proposed benefits are limited to high-temperature sliding and may not occur at lower temperatures or under non-sliding conditions.
